XK-1001-ALFA-9273-NEEDLE

The codebase is largely repetitive (the same 12 service modules are duplicated across shards with only numeric suffixes changed), and several recurring issues are present: the `InventoryService._get_lock` method has a race condition where two threads can simultaneously check `if key not in self._locks` and create separate lock objects for the same key, defeating the purpose of per-key locking; the `PaymentWebhookHandler` deduplication is not thread-safe (no lock around `_seen_recently`) and uses a non-unique key (provider+order+amount) that would incorrectly deduplicate legitimate distinct events; the `EventBus.publish` reads `_subscribers` without holding the lock, creating a potential race with concurrent `subscribe` calls; the `AuditLog` has no thread safety on `_buffer` and never clears it after `flush()`; and the `SearchIndexWriter` performs a full linear scan on every search with no indexing, which is O(n) per query.

XK-1002-BRAVO-4418-NEEDLE

The codebase is largely duplicated across shards (v0–v37) with identical logic, which itself is a maintenance concern. Notable issues include: (1) `InventoryService._get_lock` is not thread-safe—two threads can race to create the same lock, resulting in two different lock objects for the same key and thus a data race on `StockRecord`; (2) `PaymentWebhookHandler.handle` has no locking on `_seen_recently`, making deduplication racy under concurrent webhook delivery; (3) `EventBus.publish` reads `self._subscribers` without holding the lock, so a concurrent `subscribe` call can cause a `RuntimeError` (dict changed size during iteration) or missed handlers; (4) `AuditLog.record`/`flush` are not thread-safe—concurrent calls can corrupt the buffer or double-flush; (5) `SearchIndexWriter` has no synchronization at all, making it unsafe for concurrent indexing and searching; (6) `AgentToolRouter.register_tool` mutates `_handlers` and `_in_flight` without the lock, racing with `call`.
